classification.difficultyReason: Track successive depreciated values and distinguish each year's depreciation from the cumulative loss.

content.prompt: A landlord spent $\$3400$ on vacuum cleaners for his block of home units and depreciated them for taxation purposes at $25\%$ p.a. Find their value at the end of each of the first three years, and the amount of the depreciation that the landlord could claim against his taxable income for each of those three years. Give monetary answers to the nearest cent.

answer.short:
Year 1: value $\$2550$; depreciation $\$850$.

Year 2: value $\$1912.50$; depreciation $\$637.50$.

Year 3: value $\$1434.38$; depreciation $\$478.13$.
answer.worked:
Each year the vacuum cleaners retain $75\%$ of their preceding value. Each year's depreciation is the loss during that year.

$$\begin{align*}V_1&=3400\times0.75\\V_1&=\$2550\\D_1&=3400-2550\\D_1&=\$850\\V_2&=2550\times0.75\\V_2&=\$1912.50\\D_2&=2550-1912.50\\D_2&=\$637.50\\V_3&=1912.50\times0.75\\V_3&=\$1434.375\approx\$1434.38\\D_3&=1912.50-1434.375\\D_3&=\$478.125\approx\$478.13\end{align*}$$
